text: Prabhunath Singh is a politician from Bihar, India, who served as a member of the 12th, 13th, and 14th Lok Sabha. He represented the Masrakh assembly constituency from 1985 to 1995 and the Maharajganj Lok Sabha constituency from 1998 to 2009. In 2013, he won a bypoll and remained as a Member of Parliament until 2014. Singh is a member of the Janata Dal (United) (JD(U)) and is currently serving a life imprisonment sentence in a murder case. Born in Mashrakh, Saran district, Bihar, he studied up to class-12 from Bihar University, Muzaffarpur, in 1972. His brothers, Dina Singh, Madan Singh, and Kedar Singh, are also politicians. He is married to Binda Devi, and his son, Randhir Kumar Singh, is a politician who currently serves as MLA from the Manjhi Assembly constituency but lost in the 2019 Indian general election to Janardan Singh Sigriwal of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). Before entering politics, Singh owned a brick-making factory. He won his first election as an independent candidate due to his support among Rajputs in his area. He is a four-time member of parliament from the Saran district. In the 1995 elections, he ran as a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) but left the party after losing and joined the Janata Dal (United) (JD(U)). He won elections as a JD(U) member but later joined the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) due to Nitish Kumar's dictatorship in the JD(U). He represented the Maharajganj constituency from 2004 to 2009 on the JD(U) ticket. In 2009, he contested on the JD(U) ticket but narrowly lost to Uma Shankar Singh of the RJD. After Uma Shankar Singh's death, which left the seat vacant, Singh contested on the RJD ticket and defeated JD(U)'s nominee P.K. Shahi. On 23 May 2017, Singh was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Hazaribagh Court for his involvement in the murder of MLA Ashok Singh, which occurred 22 years earlier. Singh had been elected as MLA twice and as a Lok Sabha MP four times.
